description:
About the Position

Within NWO Vidi Infra-PaX, this PhD studies coordination between public and private infrastructure actors pursuing digitalisation and sustainability. It examines competing priorities across an infrastructure ecosystem.

Research Position Overview

Use embedded case studies, interviews, documentary evidence and systems thinking to investigate governance tensions and develop findings useful to practitioners.

Research Areas

  • Infrastructure governance
  • Digitalisation and sustainability
  • Qualitative case-study research

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral employee
Salary€3,204–€4,051 gross/month; first-to-fourth-year progression
Additional pay8% holiday allowance; 8.3% year-end bonus
DurationFour years in principle: 18 months initially, then 30 months after satisfactory assessment
Programme / supportNWO Vidi Infra-PaX.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationRelevant master’s, including civil engineering, construction/project management, business, information systems or innovation studies.
Relevant skillsQualitative research interest and strong analytical English communication; Dutch is advantageous, not mandatory.
EnglishRequired; see TU Delft’s admission policy for accepted evidence and exemptions.
Specific conditionsInterviews are planned for 17 and 24 November 2026.

Application dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when verified against the official source
Deadline3 November 2026
Start dateTarget: 1 February 2027
LocationDelft, Netherlands

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 3 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  • CV: maximum two pages; cover letter: maximum one page and 400 words.
  • Include a one-minute introduction-video link. Scientific outputs are optional; reference contacts follow at interview.

Use the application button on the official advert; email enquiries do not replace an online application.

About TU Delft and the Host Faculty

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, Netherlands. This position is hosted by the Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences. Doctoral employment includes Graduate School training and supervision.

Official Link

  • TU Delft vacancy and application instructions
  • TU Delft PhD admission and English-language requirements

Application guides

  • How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.
